chunks: From him, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Yassir al-Khadim and Nadir, all together said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to us: 'If I am standing over your heads while you are eating, do not get up until you have finished. And sometimes he would call one of us, and it would be said to him,
ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette for companions when eating in the presence of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) highlights the balance between reverence and naturalness in the presence of the Imam, preventing excessive formality from disrupting communal activities. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) that prioritizes comfort and completion of acts of worship or daily needs over rigid hierarchical posturing. The Imam’s instruction to let eaters finish demonstrates his attentiveness to his companions' states, fostering a relationship of ease rather than intimidation.
